key_insight: LLM judges better distinguish unsafe clinical actions when given EHR evidence, while agent reasoning does not improve overall performance.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating EHR-connected AI agents requires checking clinical actions against patient records, not just assessing whether final answers appear correct.
method: Injected controlled errors across eight categories into verified MedAgentBench trajectories.
Evaluated six open-weight LLM judges on 416 faulty trajectories paired with correct counterparts.
Compared evidence access and combined LLM judgments with a full-EHR rule-based checker.
evidence_signal: Full-trajectory evaluation reached a discrimination score of 0.75; the original grader accepted all 38 skipped-lab-check trajectories, while combined LLM and rule-based checks detected 97% of injected faults.
watch_item: These benchmark results use injected errors and do not establish safety or reliability in real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
